sources.entry: Lynote AI Humanize Text - Open-source AI text humanization toolkit for rewriting AI drafts into natural, human-like writing. Full free web version: https://lynote.ai/ai-humanizer

summary.one_liner: Open-source Python toolkit that rewrites AI-generated drafts into more natural, human-sounding prose by chaining LLM rewrites with machine-translation hops, and logs every intermediate step.
summary.what_it_does: The standard pipeline sends input text through four steps: two LLM rewrites (Input to Chinese, then Chinese to Japanese, at temperature 1.3) followed by two machine-translation hops (Japanese to Finnish via Google Translate, then Finnish to English via Niutrans). The CLI accepts a text string or a .txt path, with --verbose to watch steps and --json to output the full trace. The README also describes advanced and focus tiers that add multi-round LLM rewriting and a detection-guided feedback loop, though those are described only at a high level. LLM calls use any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, with examples for DeepSeek, OpenRouter, Atlas Cloud and OrcaRouter. The repo also includes a n8n workflow, a Docker setup for a REST endpoint, a research training-data pipeline for a structure-first rewrite model (code and demo data only, no weights), and five showcase examples. A separate hosted service at lynote.ai and its paid Humanizer API are mentioned.
use_cases: Making an AI-generated draft read more naturally
Rewriting ChatGPT output before publishing a blog post
Batch-processing text through a self-hosted REST endpoint
Automating text rewriting in an n8n workflow
Studying how multi-step translation chains alter text
Trying a no-code humanizer without managing API keys
how_to_run: cp config/config.example.toml config/config.toml  # add your LLM and Niutrans API keys
docker compose up -d  # REST endpoint; see docs/installation.md
stack: OpenAI-compatible LLM APIs (DeepSeek default, OpenRouter, Atlas Cloud, OrcaRouter, LiteLLM)
notable: Every pipeline step is visible code and can be traced with --json output
Chains translations across distant languages (Chinese, Japanese, Finnish, English) using two different MT engines
Includes an n8n no-code workflow and a Docker REST option besides the Python CLI
Ships a research structure-first SFT and KTO training-data pipeline with 50 demo records per stage
Reports a detector verdict on five showcase samples, with explicit caveats that results are not guaranteed
caveats: Requires your own LLM API key and a Niutrans key; the default setup is not zero-config
Detection outcomes are probabilistic and the project guarantees no particular classification
Translation hops can cause technical terms and citations to drift, so output needs review where exact wording matters
Model weights and full training datasets are not included; the training pipeline is research-only
Quality metrics and the 'Overall 9.1' score come from the author's own expert evaluation and are not independently verified
